faqs.question: What is Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM)?
faqs.answer: Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) is the process of managing digital certificates throughout their entire lifespan — from issuance and deployment through renewal to revocation. It covers discovery (finding all certificates across your infrastructure), issuance (requesting and deploying new certificates), renewal (renewing before expiry to prevent outages), and revocation (revoking compromised or unused certificates). AVX CLM automates all of these steps to prevent outages, ensure compliance, and maintain security at scale.

faqs.question: What is the difference between foundational and professional courses?
faqs.answer: Foundational courses are short product overviews (8–29 minutes each) for people new to AppViewX or wanting a product refresher. They cover CLM, PKIaaS, Kubernetes, Code Signing, and SSH at a high level with videos and quizzes. Professional CLM courses are deep, hands-on modules (62–122 minutes each) for administrators and engineers who need to actively operate the platform — covering architecture, configuration, integrations, discovery, and advanced workflows. Start with foundational if you're new; move to professional once you're implementing.

faqs.question: Where should I start on the Academy?
faqs.answer: If you're new to AppViewX, start with the Foundational courses at https://academy.appviewx.com/page/foundational-courses — they give you a clear overview of CLM, PKIaaS, Kubernetes, Code Signing, and SSH in under 2 hours total. Once you have that foundation, move to the Professional CLM track (https://academy.appviewx.com/page/professional-courses) starting with 'AppViewX CLM Foundations'. If you're focused on automation and workflows, the AVX Automation track (https://academy.appviewx.com/page/avx-automation) can be taken alongside the professional courses.

faqs.question: How long does it take to complete all the courses?
faqs.answer: The Foundational track totals approximately 92 minutes across 5 courses (CLM: 17 min, PKIaaS: 26 min, Kubernetes: 8 min, Code Signing: 12 min, SSH: 29 min). The Professional CLM track totals approximately 347 minutes across 4 courses (Foundations: 62 min, Public TLS: 122 min, Private PKI: 100 min, Network Scans: 63 min). The AVX Automation track has 8 self-paced modules with no fixed durations listed. Total structured learning time is roughly 7+ hours.

faqs.question: What is PKI and what is PKIaaS?
faqs.answer: PKI (Public Key Infrastructure) is a framework that uses digital certificates to verify identities, encrypt data, and ensure trust in digital communications. It prevents fraud, secures online banking, emails, and file transfers. PKIaaS (PKI as a Service) is a cloud-delivered version of a Private Certificate Authority (CA) — AppViewX's PKIaaS lets organisations issue and manage internal certificates without building their own CA infrastructure. It supports SCEP, EST, and ACME protocols and integrates with Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) and HashiCorp Vault.

faqs.question: What is AVX AI Expert?
faqs.answer: AVX AI Expert is an AI-powered assistant built into the AppViewX platform that lets you query your certificate inventory and platform data using natural language. Instead of running manual reports, you can ask questions like 'Show me certificates expiring in the next 30 days' or 'What certificates were issued last week?' and get instant answers. It's covered in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course.

faqs.question: What is the AVX Automation track?
faqs.answer: The AVX Automation track (https://academy.appviewx.com/page/avx-automation) covers AppViewX's low-code Visual Workflow automation engine. It has 8 modules: Introduction and Form Development, Functional Palettes (Split, If/Retry, REST, Switch, Subflows), Notification Palettes (Email, Slack), User Experience Palettes, Scripting with Helper Scripts, Variables (Global and Magic), Hooks/Query Explorer/REST API, and Workflow Examples. It's ideal for PKI admins, Infosec, NetOps, SecOps, and DevOps teams who want to automate certificate workflows.

faqs.question: What is a Visual Workflow in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: A Visual Workflow is AppViewX's low-code, drag-and-drop automation builder. You assemble workflows by connecting 'palettes' (pre-built functional blocks) on a canvas — no deep programming required. Palettes handle logic (If/Retry, Switch, Split), timing (Schedule, Delay), notifications (Email, Slack), REST API calls, scripting, and more. Visual Workflows let PKI admins and security teams automate certificate operations like renewal, revocation, and provisioning across complex environments.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Windows Gateway and Integrated Gateway?
faqs.answer: In AppViewX CLM, a Windows Gateway is a dedicated Windows-based connector used specifically for integrating with Microsoft Certificate Authority (MSCA). An Integrated Gateway is a more flexible, multi-purpose connector that can handle a broader range of CA integrations. Both allow AppViewX to communicate with your internal CA infrastructure for certificate operations like enroll, renew, and revoke. The differences are covered in detail in the 'Building Visibility and Monitoring for Private PKI Certificates' professional course.

faqs.question: What are the CLM Actions I can perform in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: AppViewX CLM supports five core certificate operations: Enroll (request and issue a new certificate), Renew (renew an existing certificate before expiry), Revoke (revoke a certificate that is compromised or no longer needed), Regenerate (generate a new key pair and re-issue the certificate), and Reissue (re-issue the certificate with the same key pair). All five actions are covered in the 'Building Visibility and Monitoring for Private PKI Certificates' professional course.

faqs.question: What is the Cloud Connector?
faqs.answer: The Cloud Connector is an AppViewX component that enables connectivity between the AppViewX platform and cloud environments. It handles the communication required for certificate discovery, management, and automation in cloud-based infrastructure. Its requirements and installation procedure are covered in the 'AppViewX CLM Foundations' professional course.

faqs.question: What is LDAP integration in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) integration in AppViewX enables synchronisation with your organisation's directory services (such as Active Directory) for centralised user and group management. Instead of managing users manually in AppViewX, you can sync users and roles from your LDAP directory, streamlining access control and governance. LDAP configuration is covered in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course.

faqs.question: What is SSO and how do I configure it in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: SSO (Single Sign-On) allows users to authenticate to AppViewX using their existing enterprise credentials, eliminating the need for separate AppViewX passwords. AppViewX supports SAML and OIDC protocols for SSO. Configuration is covered step-by-step in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course. SSO is recommended for enterprise deployments to improve security and simplify user access.

faqs.question: What is a CT Log Scan (Certificate Transparency Log Scan)?
faqs.answer: A Certificate Transparency (CT) Log Scan allows AppViewX to discover certificates issued for your domains by public Certificate Authorities and logged in the publicly available CT logs. This gives you visibility into externally issued certificates that you may not be tracking internally — including certificates issued by shadow IT or unknown parties. CT Log Scans are covered in the 'Building Visibility and Monitoring for Public TLS Certificates' professional course.

faqs.question: What format are the courses in?
faqs.answer: Most courses combine video lessons, quiz questions, and downloadable PDFs. Foundational courses are primarily video-based with embedded quizzes at the end. Professional CLM courses include longer video modules, hands-on walkthroughs, and assessment quizzes. The AVX Automation track is self-paced video content. All courses also include a rating step so learners can provide feedback.

faqs.question: Who are the professional CLM courses designed for?
faqs.answer: The Professional CLM track is designed for: New AppViewX users looking for a hands-on starting point, IT managers evaluating the platform's capabilities, and security teams transitioning from manual certificate tracking to automated lifecycle management. Within the track, later courses target PKI and certificate administrators, security engineers, DevOps and platform engineers, compliance and risk management professionals, and PKI architects designing global certificate strategies.

faqs.question: What is RBAC in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) in AppViewX controls who can perform which operations on the platform. It ensures the right people have the right level of access — for example, a read-only auditor role vs. a full certificate administrator role. RBAC is a core platform feature introduced in the CLM Foundations course and applies across all modules including certificate operations, workflow management, and platform administration.

faqs.question: What is the Insights Dashboard in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: The Insights Dashboard in AppViewX provides real-time visibility into your certificate posture, risks, and operational trends. It aggregates data across your certificate inventory to help you track certificates by expiry status, issuing CA, compliance state, and more. It's covered in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course alongside Alerts and Logs.

faqs.question: What is a CA Scan?
faqs.answer: A CA Scan in AppViewX queries a connected Certificate Authority directly to retrieve all certificates issued by that CA — including ones that may not have been discovered through network scans. This gives you a complete, authoritative inventory of certificates issued by your internal CAs and helps identify unmanaged or risky certificates. CA Scans are covered in the 'Building Visibility and Monitoring for Private PKI Certificates' professional course.

faqs.question: What are Certificate Attributes?
faqs.answer: Certificate Attributes in AppViewX are custom metadata fields you can add to certificates beyond the standard fields (like subject, expiry, and issuer). They allow you to tag certificates with business context — such as the owning team, application name, environment (prod/dev/staging), or compliance classification. Custom attributes are covered in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course.

faqs.question: What are Magic Variables in Visual Workflows?
faqs.answer: Magic Variables in AppViewX Visual Workflows are dynamic, context-aware variables that automatically capture and pass data between workflow palettes. They allow you to reference the output of one step as the input to another without manual mapping, making workflows more flexible and data-driven. Magic Variables are covered in two parts in the 'Visual Workflows: Variables' module of the AVX Automation track.

faqs.question: What is a Subflow in Visual Workflows?
faqs.answer: A Subflow is a reusable workflow that can be called from within another workflow — similar to a function or subroutine in programming. Subflows help you modularise complex automations, avoid duplication, and maintain consistency across multiple workflows. For example, you might create a subflow for 'send expiry alert' that multiple different workflows all call. Subflows are covered in 'Visual Workflows: Working with Functional Palettes'.

faqs.question: What are the prerequisites for the AVX Automation courses?
faqs.answer: The first module (Visual Workflows: Introduction and Form Development) has no listed prerequisites. Subsequent modules recommend completing earlier modules in sequence, particularly the Introduction module which establishes foundational workflow concepts. The Automation track is designed for PKI admins, Infosec, NetOps, SecOps, and DevOps teams — basic familiarity with IT operations is helpful.

faqs.question: What is a Network Scan in AppViewX?
faqs.answer: A Network Scan in AppViewX actively scans your network infrastructure to discover certificates across servers, load balancers, and endpoints. It identifies certificates regardless of how they were issued — even ones not managed through AppViewX. Configuration includes setting scan targets, ports, protocols, and permissions to ensure thorough coverage without disrupting production traffic. Network Scans are covered in the 'Discovering Certificates with Network Scans and Platform Integrations' professional course.

faqs.question: Are certifications available on the Academy?
faqs.answer: Certifications are coming soon! AppViewX is developing industry-recognised certification programmes across the Foundational, Professional, and Automation tracks — including digital badges you can share on LinkedIn and your résumé. You can sign up on the Academy homepage to be notified the moment certifications go live.

faqs.question: What is the difference between CLM and PKIaaS?
faqs.answer: AVX CLM (Certificate Lifecycle Management) manages the full lifecycle of SSL/TLS certificates across your enterprise — discovery, tracking, renewal, and revocation regardless of which CA issued them. AVX PKIaaS (PKI as a Service) is specifically about running your own Private Certificate Authority in the cloud — it issues internal certificates using SCEP, EST, and ACME protocols. In practice, many organisations use both: PKIaaS to issue internal certificates, and CLM to manage the full lifecycle of both internally and externally issued certificates.
